title: Heat Pump Rebates in Guelph 2026: Rebates by Fuel and What the Contractor Files
desc: Guelph heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: $500 per ton for gas, $1,250 per ton for electric, oil, propane or wood, and Alectra as the electric utility.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Guelph has 56,480 households, 66% of them owners. The rebate is per ton by current fuel, and the contractor files the paperwork.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Guelph
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 49% of households in detached houses, 69% in an eligible type and 4.7% reporting a home needing major repairs. 44% live in homes built before 1981 and 10,940 are owner-occupied detached houses of that age. 12% live in tall apartments and 14% in low-rise buildings.

Guelph's electric utility is Alectra Utilities, which took over Guelph Hydro. Alectra does not set the heat pump rebate. Ask whether Alectra offers anything on your bill, and whether it can be combined.

A rebate for a 2-ton air-source system is $1,000 for a gas home or $2,500 for an electric one. The ton figure is the rated heating capacity at 8.3°C divided by 12,000 BTU/h, taken from the NRCan listing. Ask the contractor to show the listing for the exact model and outdoor unit pairing.

The post-installation application includes a photo of the installed thermostat. Ask which thermostat controls the system and how it interacts with any backup heat. With a gas furnace kept as backup, the controls decide when each heat source runs.

Within 30 days of the install the contractor submits the final itemized invoice, photos of the installed equipment and thermostat, and installation details. For a Guelph home with several outdoor units, each unit needs its own record. The cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

A home that already uses a heat pump for space heating is not eligible. A Guelph owner whose only cooling is an air conditioner should ask the program how the unit is classed. The heat pump system that is installed must include all indoor and outdoor components and be capable of heating and cooling year-round.
claim_steps: Find the rated capacity of the model you are quoted.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
